definitions.explanation: Communicated by speaking rather than in writing. Used as a noun modifier (with の) to describe instructions, agreements, explanations, and other forms of communication that are delivered orally.

examples.japanese: {口頭|こうとう}で{説明|せつめい}する。
{口頭|こうとう}{試験|しけん}は{来週|らいしゅう}の{月曜日|げつようび}に{行|おこな}われる。
examples.english: The oral examination will be held next Monday.

examples.japanese: {書面|しょめん}ではなく{口頭|こうとう}での{約束|やくそく}だったので、{証拠|しょうこ}が{残|のこ}っていない。
examples.english: Since it was a verbal promise rather than a written one, there is no evidence left.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{口頭|こうとう}{試験|しけん} (oral examination)
・{口頭|こうとう}で{伝|つた}える (convey orally)
・{口頭|こうとう}{弁論|べんろん} (oral argument, court hearing)
・{口頭|こうとう}{注意|ちゅうい} (verbal warning)

Almost always used as a modifier with の or in compound nouns. The contrast is with {書面|しょめん} (written) or {文書|ぶんしょ} (document). Not to be confused with the homophone {高等|こうとう} (high-level, advanced).
